articles.headline: Bubble Watch Heading into Bristol as the Chase Cut Approaches
articles.dek: An analysis of the remaining playoff contenders and the mathematical scenarios unfolding before race 18 of 20.
articles.body:
The regular season concludes in two weeks with the seventeenth and eighteenth rounds deciding the final playoff grid. With the standings tightly bunched around the cutoff line, attention turns to Sean Corr, Derek White, Tyler Payne, and Kolby Newman as they fight for survival in the 2029 simulation series.

Nicholas Hoggeton currently leads the overall standings with 2801 points. Robbie Kennealy sits second with 2771 points and two wins, followed closely by Andrew Patterson with 2738 points and two wins. William Faison, Alfie Denley, Eric Caudell, Daniel Stavchanksy, and Brenden Queen occupy positions four through eight.

The bubble battle centers on ninth through sixteenth place. Sean Corr holds ninth with 2380 points. Derek White sits tenth with 2373 points and two victories. Tyler Payne follows in eleventh with 2337 points, while Kolby Newman is twelfth at 2309 points. Vincent Crook holds thirteenth with 2304 points and two wins. Karson Mitchell stands fourteenth with 2251 points, Caleb Guerrier is fifteenth with 2225 points, and Willie Mullins rounds out the top sixteen with 2193 points.

Derek White recently demonstrated strong short track form at Indianapolis Raceway Park by charging from twenty-fourth to seventh to claim biggest mover honors, boosting his reputation to 70. That performance provides crucial momentum as the tour heads to Bristol Motor Speedway for the Bush's Beans 200.

The model lists win odds for the upcoming short track event with Robbie Kennealy at 15 percent, Nicholas Hoggeton at 14 percent, Andrew Patterson at 13 percent, Alfie Denley at 10 percent, Eric Caudell at 9 percent, and Daniel Stavchanksy at 6 percent. Bubble drivers must capitalize on stage points and avoid mechanical attrition to secure their postseason berths.
articles.author: Ross Delgado

articles.headline: Kennealy Dominates at Indianapolis to Claim Second Win of the Season
articles.dek: Robbie Kennealy navigated fourteen caution periods to secure victory in the LiUNA! 150 presented by IDEAL Garage Door at Lucas Oil Indianapolis Raceway Park.
articles.body:
Robbie Kennealy drove his number 41 machine to victory lane in Race 13 of the NASCAR ARCA Menards Series season, holding off Karson Mitchell by 1.073 seconds in a race slowed down by fourteen cautions. Kennealy started ninth on the grid and worked his way to the front, leading 136 of the 300 laps at the short track.

Karson Mitchell charged hard from an eighth-place starting spot, leading 48 laps before settling for second. Pole sitter Andrew Patterson led 33 laps and completed the podium in third. Nicholas Hoggeton recovered from a sixteenth-place start to finish fourth, leading 26 laps, while Brenden Queen rounded out the top five after leading 19 laps.

The race featured heavy attrition with fourteen cautions interrupting the rhythm. Several drivers failed to finish, including Ron Vandermeir Jr. due to overheating, and Wesley Slimp, Nick Apollo, Samuel Riggs, and Presley Sorah who were caught up in accidents. James Baker also exited early with engine failure. Derek White put on a driving exhibition, charging from twenty-fourth on the grid to finish seventh, earning the biggest mover honors of the afternoon.

In the championship standings, Nicholas Hoggeton maintains his hold on the top spot with 2043 points. Eric Caudell sits second with 1991 points and one win, while Kennealy's victory moves him up to third with 1946 points and two wins. Andrew Patterson is fourth with 1945 points and one win, and William Faison rounds out the top five with 1943 points and two wins.

The ARCA Menards Series heads to the next round on the 20-race calendar as the championship battle intensifies down the stretch.
articles.author: Jamie Kowalski

articles.headline: Midseason Power Rankings: Caudell Holds Top Spot As Field Nears New Hampshire
articles.dek: A look at the top five drivers in the sim standings at the midway point of the 2029 season.
articles.body:
Eric Caudell sits atop the championship standings heading into the second half of the twenty-nine sim racing season. With 1252 points and one victory, Caudell has maintained remarkable consistency through the first eight events. The simulator gives him a thirteen percent win probability for the upcoming short track race at New Hampshire.

William Faison remains his closest challenger in second place with 1218 points and a single win. Faison has quietly put together a string of solid finishes to keep the pressure on the standings leader. Nicholas Hoggeton holds third overall with 1203 points, staying in the hunt without visiting victory lane yet this year.

Brenden Queen occupies the fourth position at 1197 points and one win. Queen boasts a simulator win odd of nine percent for the upcoming Herrs Snacks 200. Rounding out the top five, Daniel Stavchanksy has accumulated 1177 points and enters the weekend with an eleven percent model win projection.

articles.headline: Patterson Charges from 24th to Win Daytona Season Opener
articles.dek: Andrew Patterson dominated the second half at Daytona, leading 99 laps to claim the General Tire 200.
articles.body:
DAYTONA BEACH, Fla. — Andrew Patterson drove from deep in the field to win the General Tire 200 at Daytona International Speedway on Wednesday, capturing the 2029 ARCA Menards Series season opener. Patterson, who rolled off 24th on the 28-car grid, methodically worked his way through the pack before taking control at the front, holding off Eric Caudell by 0.448 seconds at the line.

Patterson was the class of the field once he found clear air. The driver of the No. 40 car led 99 of the event's 188 laps, asserting command on a superspeedway surface that punished attrition. Nine caution periods interrupted the pace throughout the afternoon, eliminating seven cars due to crashes and mechanical failures, but Patterson consistently controlled restarts from the point.

Caudell put together a strong effort in the closing laps. Starting 12th, Caudell led 20 laps in the No. 7 machine and kept Patterson within striking distance during the final green-flag run, but lacked the drafting help required to mount a serious challenge before the checkered flag. Daniel Stavchansky followed closely in third after leading 17 laps, while William Faison gained 16 spots from his 20th starting position to finish fourth. Nicholas Hoggeton rounded out the top five with 14 laps led.

The race proved costly for several contenders early in the year. Wesley Slimp, Vincent Crook, and Ron Vandermeir Jr. dropped out after falling victim to the Damaged Vehicle Policy, while Presley Sorah saw his day end early in an accident. Mechanical gremlins also sidelined Samuel Riggs with overheating issues, Ed Pompa with engine trouble, and Atsz Minyoung with a broken transmission.

Further back in the top ten, Robbie Kennealy matched Patterson's aggression in traffic, climbing from 28th on the grid to finish sixth while leading nine laps. Brenden Queen led eight laps on his way to seventh, with Tyler Payne, Caleb Guerrier, and Willie Mullins completing the top ten.

With the victory, Patterson leaves Daytona with the early points lead in the 20-race campaign. The field established strong baseline pace, though the attrition rate shows how unforgiving Daytona remains for teams still sorting out their equipment.
articles.author: Jamie Kowalski

posts.text: Fourteen yellow flags turned a short track slugfest into an absolute marathon. Kennealy had the dominant piece leading 136, but sitting through all those cleanups after working 50 hours this week tested my patience.

He survived and moved up twelve spots while others piled into the wall young man.
ok and? zero laps led

Had Patterson slotted as my anchor from the pole. Led 33 laps and grabbed third, but Mitchell stealing second on that last restart cost me the top tier payout.

Sean Corr quietly rolling from 20th up to 12th kept me glued to the timing monitor. Clean run amidst chaos.
Derek White gained 17 positions tonight (started 24th, finished 7th), leading 13 laps. Biggest mover in the LiUNA 150.

still led 13 laps which is 13 more than McCoy Behnke who started 11th and managed to fall back to 14th 💀

interviews.quote: Starting twenty-fourth makes for a long day at a short track, but we kept digging and picked them off one by one.
We came from eighth and had a real shot at it at the end. Just needed a little more on the final restart to get by the forty-one.
That car was dialed in all day. Fourteen cautions is a lot to handle, but the guys gave me a setup that stayed under me.
Coming from 28th to sixth is a good salvage job, but we had to dodge a lot of tore up equipment today. The car was tight in traffic. We got lucky a few times on those restarts.

We had a shot there at the end, but the 40 car just covered every run we tried to build. Second hurts when you lead laps, but it's a solid start for our program. We'll take the points and keep building.
Starting 24th here isn't ideal, but the car had serious speed once the pack opened up. We had the horsepower and just stayed disciplined working the lines. Clean air was everything at the end.

john verstappen.name: John Verstappen
john verstappen.bio: John Verstappen grew up working on dairy equipment in rural Wisconsin before helping his uncle prep street stocks at the local half-mile oval. He spent seven years running regional touring divisions, slowly building a reputation as a clean, low-maintenance driver who rarely tore up equipment. Now piloting the 98 for Shearer Speed Racing, he approaches race weekends with a quiet, blue-collar work ethic.

vincent crook.name: Vincent Crook
vincent crook.bio: Vincent Crook started racing go-karts on temporary asphalt setups in Pacific Northwest industrial parks. After years of self-funding his late model efforts through a commercial plumbing business, he finally caught a break in regional stock car touring series. He brings a gritty, pragmatic approach to the 89 entry for Rise Racing with Earnhardt-Shearer Racing.

kolby newman.name: Kolby Newman
kolby newman.bio: Kolby Newman spent his teens racing dirt modifieds across the Midwest circuits with his father acting as crew chief and engine builder. He transitioned to asphalt via regional developmental combines, showing steady car control on intermediate tracks. Now driving the 99 for Maples Motorsports, he is still learning how to manage full-distance race strategies.

caleb guerrier.name: Caleb Guerrier
caleb guerrier.bio: Caleb Guerrier grew up around swamp buggy races before pivoting to asphalt street stock racing in his early twenties. He bounced through various underfunded independent teams for over a decade, keeping rides afloat with sheer mechanical persistence. Currently piloting the 06 for Wayne Peterson Motorsports, he acts as an on-track veteran who keeps expectations grounded.

tyler payne.name: Tyler Payne
tyler payne.bio: Tyler Payne started in Midwest quarter midgets before moving up through regional asphalt stock car series. He balanced college classes in mechanical engineering with weekend travel to various short tracks across the Great Lakes. Piloting the 79 for ACR Motorsports, he approaches car setups with a technical mindset and calculated execution.

william faison.name: William Faison
william faison.bio: William Faison spent his early years working in coastal boatyards before funding his own hobby stock racing hobby. He spent over a decade quietly climbing the regional ladder without the benefit of major sponsorship backing. Driving the 86 for Clubb Racing Inc., he relies on his extensive endurance racing background to manage worn-out tires.

daniel stavchanksy.name: Daniel Stavchanksy
daniel stavchanksy.bio: Daniel Stavchanksy grew up racing local asphalt legends cars while studying industrial fabrication. He progressed through regional developmental series by securing localized backing from heavy manufacturing firms. Now driving the 03 for Clubb Racing Inc., he brings a methodical and cautious approach to every race.

atsz minyoung.name: Atsz Minyoung
atsz minyoung.bio: Atsz Minyoung started driving ice-races on frozen lakes before relocating to the lower forty-eight to pursue pavement stock car racing. He worked as a fabricator for various regional teams while scraping together funds for occasional starts. Behind the wheel of the 12 for Fast Track Racing, he is recognized for car control in low-grip conditions.

mccoy behnke.name: McCoy Behnke
mccoy behnke.bio: McCoy Behnke spent his youth wrenching on pickup trucks and racing local asphalt bombers in Big Sky country. He transitioned to regional touring series after winning a series of local short track championships. Driving the 24 for SPS Racing, he is a quiet competitor focused on bringing the car home in one piece.
